$comment: A LANGUAGE prior. Data only, no code. Staged here for transfer to eoPriors; nothing in packages/ may hardcode any of it.

provenance.source: APiCS Online (Atlas of Pidgin and Creole Language Structures), Survey chapter 17, 'Nigerian Pidgin', author Nicholas Faraclas, https://apics-online.info/surveys/17 — a real academic typological database, not a general-audience summary. Corroborated by naija.guru's 'Negation in Nigerian Pidgin' grammar page and, for the anterior/completive form, an example sentence in a university pidgin-creole teaching handout (martinschaefer.info).
provenance.built_by: hand-curated from real cited sources, deliberately minimal rather than padded with recalled-but-uncited items

attested.period: Not stated explicitly in the survey chapter itself — it names no fieldwork years. Triangulated from Faraclas's biography and adjacent publications (not a directly-quoted date): graduate fieldwork substantially in the 1980s (PhD, UC Berkeley, 1989; a related 1986 publication, 'Reading and Writing Nigerian Pidgin', Rivers Readers Project, Port Harcourt), consolidated into his 1996 Routledge descriptive grammar, then condensed a second time into this 2013 APiCS survey chapter (Michaelis, Maurer, Haspelmath & Huber, eds.). Read as: description reflects data gathered roughly the 1980s-1990s, republished/synthesized in 2013 — not a fresh 2013 fieldwork date.
attested.basis: Grounded 2026-08-19: the staged survey text itself (no explicit date), corroborated by web search of Faraclas's biography and bibliography (PhD 1989; 1986 orthography publication; 1996 Routledge grammar) and the 2013 APiCS edited-volume publication date. The specific decade attribution is triangulated, not directly quoted from a primary source stating a fieldwork period — treat as well-supported but inferential.
attested.confidence: medium — inferred from biography and publication history, not a stated fieldwork-date sentence

region.detail: The survey chapter presents the no/neva negation facts as flat, unqualified 'Nigerian Pidgin' facts — no regional flag anywhere in section 7. But the chapter's own companion structure dataset (apics-online.info/contributions/17) states its actual empirical anchor directly: 'the default lect... utilized for the descriptions... is that used by... the metropolitan area of the city of Port Harcourt... in the southeast of Nigeria' — not the Warri/Sapele 'deep' variety the chapter's own sociolinguistic section (§3) foregrounds as the most fluent register. No source found (staged file or web search) documents whether the no/neva negation STRUCTURE itself actually varies between Lagos, Warri/Delta, Port Harcourt, and Benin City varieties — what IS documented as varying regionally is phonology, substrate-language lexical borrowing intensity, and specific discourse particles (e.g. the Yoruba-derived tag 'shebi', attested elsewhere but reported absent from Port Harcourt data) — none of that is this specific negation feature. This is a genuine, disclosed gap, not a claim of either pan-Nigerian stability or documented regional variation.
region.basis: Local file 11-multi-language/dialects-pidgins-creoles/apics/surveys/survey-17-nigerian-pidgin.txt (§3, §7, read in full) cross-checked against a direct fetch of apics-online.info/contributions/17 (Port Harcourt attribution quoted verbatim). Secondary, not independently verified by direct fetch: Faraclas's 1996 grammar described in search results as based on data 'collected... throughout South Eastern Nigeria'; Dagmar Deuber (2005), 'Nigerian Pidgin in Lagos', examines verbal negation as a register-variation (formality) axis within Lagos specifically — a different question from cross-regional variation, and not independently confirmed here.

notes: negation: the free-standing negation particle(s) that precede a finite verb — the same slot perceiver/text/relations.js's negation-before-verb window already checks (before the verb, within the clause), and priors.js::NEGATION_WORDS holds for English (giver lang/en).

'no' is the GENERAL preverbal negator: 'A no bay nyam' = 'I didn't buy yams' (APiCS Survey 17). Also negates nouns ('no wód' = 'no way'), which this prior does not attempt to capture — only the preverbal-negator use is in scope for this mechanism.

'neva' and 'never' are recorded as attested orthographic variants of ONE negative completive/anterior particle — it replaces the affirmative 'no...don' construction ('A neva bay nyam' = 'I haven't bought yams'), a genuinely distinct grammatical slot from bare 'no', not merely a spelling variant of English 'never'.

Consumed by perceiver/text/relations.js::discoverRelationVocab and ::extractRelations via the injected `negationWords` option (a Set) — the same seam bin/priors/lang/en.json's own abbreviations already opened on spans.js::splitSentences, and bin/priors/lang/eu.json (Basque) already uses.

Deliberately EXCLUDED, each checked and refused rather than assumed: 'abi' is a sentence-final tag-question/pragmatic particle (Yoruba-derived, 'isn't it?'), not a negator, confirmed against multiple sources describing its pragmatic-marker function. 'nothing'/'nobody'/'nowhere'/'none of' are negative indefinite pronouns/determiners (compositional 'no' + a noun), not free-standing negation triggers themselves — the same distinction English's own NEGATION_WORDS list already draws by excluding 'nothing'/'nobody'. APiCS Survey 17 itself states Nigerian Pidgin has NO negative concord (unlike, say, AAVE) and uses 'eni' ('any') for negative-polarity indefinites, not a distinct negator. 'no be'/'no dey'/'no go'/'no fit' are not separate negators — they are 'no' plus an ordinary TAM auxiliary or verb ('be'/'dey'/'go'/'fit'), already covered by the single entry 'no'.

Measured against real material: eval/vendored-prior-eval.md in the-fold repo records the before/after result of injecting this file's `negation` set against real prose fetched from pcm.wikipedia.org (8+ full articles, ~117K characters) — negation particles confirmed present in the real fetched text before this file was built, e.g. 'Fela mama no sopot di Oyinbo rul ova Naija' ('Fela's mother did not support the British rule over Nigeria').

Added 2026-08-19 (schema NegationPrior@2): the `attested`/`region` blocks above are the grounded answer to 'chronologically stamped, regional when possible' — the honest finding is a real citation gap, not a clean date/place. pcm.wikipedia.org's own contributors are not identifiably Port-Harcourt-anchored (Wikipedia editors are unlocated by default), so the material this prior was VALIDATED against and the material its NEGATION FACT is EMPIRICALLY GROUNDED in (Faraclas's Port Harcourt-anchored fieldwork) are not confirmed to be the same regional register — both are real, cited, and Nigerian Pidgin, but their regional relationship to each other is not established, and is stated here rather than silently assumed.
